instructions:
## Assistant's notes (may be inaccurate)

Use these only for choices the user confirmed in the conversation that are missing from their request below. Never add a feature, database, framework, tool or deployment step that is not in the user's request; where these notes disagree with it, the user's request wins.

Build a web app with a new GUI. Generate the application code for that GUI.

## The user's original request, verbatim

This is the authority. Where the summary above is shorter or differs, this text wins.

Create a web app called "Recommendations Tracker" to keep all the recommendations in one place, organised by type.

Class diagram: one class named Recommendation, no other classes or associations:

title: str (required)
category: enumeration RecommendationCategory with values Book, Film, Place, Article, Recipe, Restaurant, Other (required)
status: enumeration RecommendationStatus with values ToTry, Done, Dropped (required)
note: str (optional)
added_on: date (required)
GUI diagram: three screens, Home (main page), Recommendations and Add recommendation.

Navigation bar on all screens: the app title on the left, and exactly three items on the right: Home, Recommendations, Add recommendation. No other items or duplicate links in the bar.

Home screen, from top to bottom:

A banner with the title "Recommendations Tracker", the subtitle "All your recommendations, organised by type", the total number of recommendations, and one "Add recommendation" button with clear spacing from the text.
A "Browse by category" section with seven cards (Book, Film, Place, Article, Recipe, Restaurant, Other). Each card shows an icon, the category name, the number of recommendations, and how many are To try and Done. Clicking a card opens the Recommendations screen showing only that category.
A "Recently added" section with the last 5 recommendations (title, category, date), and a friendly message when there are none yet. This section appears once.
A vertical bar chart titled "Distribution by category", with one bar per category (all seven always shown, including those with 0), a different colour per bar, and the count written above each bar. The Y axis must show whole numbers only (0, 1, 2, 3...), never decimals such as 0.5 or 0.25, even when there are only one or two recommendations. Set the axis to integer ticks with a minimum of 0 and a step of 1.
Recommendations screen: a page title and short subtitle, filters for category and status, one "Add recommendation" button, and a table bound to Recommendation showing all five attributes, with Edit and Delete, sorting and pagination.

Add recommendation screen: a form bound to Recommendation with dropdowns for category and status and a date input for added_on, and a Save button.

Design: modern, clean and appealing. Use a soft indigo-to-sky-blue gradient on the banner, a light neutral page background, white rounded cards with a subtle shadow and a gentle hover lift, and generous, even spacing between sections. Use a harmonious palette for the categories and chart bars: indigo, sky blue, teal, amber, coral, violet, slate. Use one consistent font, and highlight the current page in the navigation bar. No authentication and no agents.

This later request takes precedence where it changes earlier requirements.
